Damp found: Elevated moisture readings were recorded to sections of the internal wall surfaces that include {MAIN_WALL_DAMP_LOCATION} (see section J1 - Risk to Building; see section J3 - Risk to people).

Penetrating damp: This may have been affected by penetrating damp probably caused by {MAIN_WALL_PENETRATING_DAMP_CAUSED_BY}. When the problem has been resolved, the wall may need to be repaired. Repair options: The source of the moisture should be identified and remedied as a priority. Once the source of moisture has been eliminated and the affected walls have been allowed sufficient time to dry naturally, any damaged plaster, decorations or other finishes should be repaired or replaced as necessary. The affected area should then be monitored to ensure that the dampness does not recur.
Rising damp: This may have been affected by rising damp probably caused by {MAIN_WALL_RISING_DAMP_CAUSED_BY}. When the problem has been resolved, the wall may need to be repaired.

Install drain guttering: Because the external ground levels are high in relation to the building, the damp-proof course (DPC) may be bridged in places, allowing moisture to penetrate the walls (see section J1 - Risk to Building). External ground levels should be reduced where practicable to maintain an appropriate clearance below the damp-proof course. Where this is not feasible, suitable drainage measures, such as a French drain or gravel-filled drainage channel, may be appropriate to improve surface water drainage and reduce the risk of moisture penetration. A suitably qualified contractor should advise on the most appropriate remedial solution.

Investigate cause: The source of moisture cannot be confirmed during a visual inspection. You should instruct a suitably qualified contractor to investigate the cause of the dampness and carry out any necessary repairs to prevent further moisture penetration. Following completion of the repairs, the affected walls should be allowed to dry before any replastering, redecoration or replacement of finishes is undertaken. Premature redecoration may result in the recurrence of staining or damage if residual moisture remains within the wall.

DPC Treatment noted: I noted evidence of damp proof course treatment, ventilation apparatus, ventilation holes, in the property. You should ask your legal adviser to check whether there has been a dampness problem before and if a valid guarantee or warranty covers this work (See Section I2 - Guarantees). If not, you should ask an appropriately qualified person to inspect the property, assess its condition and identify what repairs are required. Once the repairs have been completed, this person should issue a certificate of 'structural worthiness'. You should ask your insurance company if this problem would affect your ability to get insurance cover for this property.

The inspection undertaken for this survey is not intended to identify or confirm the presence of asbestos. According to the Health and Safety Executive (HSE), asbestos-containing materials do not normally present a significant health risk if they are in good condition and remain undisturbed. However, if such materials are damaged, drilled, cut, or otherwise disturbed, asbestos fibres may be released, posing a health hazard and requiring specialist management or removal. These regulations impose strict requirements on the assessment, handling, removal, and disposal of asbestos, which can significantly increase the cost of repair, maintenance, or alteration works. If asbestos is suspected or confirmed, your legal adviser should make appropriate enquiries regarding any previous asbestos surveys, removal works, or management records relating to the property. Further advice should be obtained where refurbishment is proposed.
